audit.whatIsWrong: Both layers read Skill / Skill / Skill / Ziggs / Skill / Skill / Ziggs, which gives Trundle nothing — but two of the whys claim a stage outright: whys[2] calls level 3 "your first real threat window and the only level range where you can realistically kill him", and whys[4] says at level 6 "he cannot out-damage a tanky Trundle healing inside Frozen Domain once his resistances are gone".
audit.why: Those are not descriptions of an even stage. Trundle loses this lane overall at 48.46% over 130 games, and the honest shape is a Ziggs poke lane with two Trundle windows cut into it at 3 and 6 — which is exactly what the rest of the page argues. Leaving both as Skill hides the only two moments a Trundle is supposed to act on.
audit.corrected: Trundle at level 3 and level 6; the rest of the chart stays as it is.

audit.whatIsWrong: spikes[3] and whys[6] describe the late game as unanswerable siege with no numbers, and whys[6] adds that "your Subjugate loses value against a squishy AP carry".
audit.why: Mega Inferno Bomb is 120/95/70 seconds at 5000 range — the number is what makes his global pressure schedulable rather than constant. And the claim that Subjugate is weak into a squishy is the same templated error that appears in the Teemo and Vayne entries: the ultimate deals 20/25/30% of the target's maximum health as magic damage and heals Trundle for the same amount, which on a mage's health bar is a larger share of the fight than any resistance steal would be.
audit.corrected: Mega Inferno Bomb 120/95/70s at 5000 range. Subjugate is strongest, not weakest, against a health bar like his.

audit.whatIsWrong: The two layers directly contradict each other on whether Ziggs can escape. The full layer tracks Satchel Charge as "His knockback + self-peel escape" in breakdown.cooldowns, dosFull[0], report[5] and the tldr. The content layer says the opposite: spikes[1] "he has no defensive ability to escape the drain" and `mid` "He has no dash, no invulnerability, no mobility spell".
audit.why: The full layer is right and the content layer is dangerous. Riot's text for Satchel Charge is explicit — the explosion knocks enemies away, and "Ziggs is also knocked away, but takes no damage". It is a self-displacement escape on 20/18/16/14/12 seconds. A Trundle told Ziggs has no mobility will commit the level-6 all-in into a full Satchel Charge and lose both his ultimate and the trade.
audit.corrected: Satchel Charge (20/18/16/14/12s, 1000 range) knocks Ziggs clear as well as you. The all-in starts after he spends it.

audit.whatIsWrong: Hexplosive Minefield is described in `mid` as something that makes any walk-up cost "the full zone tick damage", and in whys[3] and wants.foe[2] as an approach-denial tool, with no mention of its own limiter.
audit.why: Riot's text says successive mine detonations on the SAME target deal reduced damage. That inverts the correct movement: walking a straight line through the field costs far less than picking around it, because each additional mine hits for less. It is also a flat 16 seconds at every rank, so unlike his Q it never gets more frequent. Short Fuse has the opposite property and is also unstated — its cooldown is reduced whenever Ziggs uses an ability, so his empowered auto arrives faster the more he casts.
audit.corrected: Hexplosive Minefield (flat 16s): repeat detonations on the same target are reduced — walk straight through. Short Fuse speeds up with every ability he casts.

audit.whatIsWrong: wants.you[0] says "Chomp's attack-speed steal", wants.you[1] calls Pillar of Ice "the knock-up into slow", and whys[4] and `mid` say Subjugate's "first cast strips half his MR".
audit.why: Chomp saps Attack Damage — which against a mage is close to irrelevant anyway, so the line was selling the wrong reason to walk up. Pillar of Ice makes impassable terrain and slows; there is no knock-up in it. And Subjugate is a single cast that takes 40%, not half, with the amount stolen doubling over the following 4 seconds — "first cast" implies a second one that does not exist.
audit.corrected: Chomp: AD sap and a movement slow. Pillar of Ice: terrain plus a slow. Subjugate: one cast, 40%, doubling over 4s.

audit.whatIsWrong: Packet defect confirmed: no cooldown figure appears anywhere in either layer, and breakdown.cooldowns names Satchel Charge without one.
audit.why: Bouncing Bomb 6/5.5/5/4.5/4s at 850 range, Satchel Charge 20/18/16/14/12s, Hexplosive Minefield a flat 16s, Mega Inferno Bomb 120/95/70s, against Chomp's flat 3.5s at 300 range and Pillar of Ice's 21s. The pairing that matters is Satchel Charge at 20 against Pillar of Ice at 21: they are the same cooldown, so the walk-up you win is the one where he satchelled first.
audit.corrected: Numbers added to breakdown.cooldowns, phases[2], phases[4], report[5], dosFull[0], dontsFull[1], spikes, early, mid, late and two whys.

audit.why: report[8] starts Doran's Shield into his poke and takes Mercury's Treads against an all-magic kit, which is right, and no Ziggs ability heals so the absence of anti-heal is correct. I left itemization alone.

Both packet suspectNames — "Use Pillar of Ice" and "Lay Hexplosive Minefield" — are false positives on the names. One derived-flag misfire I deliberately did not propagate: Satchel Charge carries a percentHealth flag, and _missing-interactions.json therefore raises resistances-invalidated for this matchup, but Riot's description gives no max-health component against champions — the percentage language belongs to hexploding vulnerable turrets. I trusted the description and wrote nothing about Ziggs bypassing resistances.

edits.before: At levels 1-2 you are farming under a bomb barrage — Ziggs's Q Bouncing Bomb outranges every ability you have, and his Short Fuse empowered auto hits you every few seconds if you contest the wave at the same spot. Accept that. Use Q Chomp on the wave for passive King's Tribute healing to offset the poke, and position so his Bouncing Bomb has to arc over minions to hit you, reducing his accuracy. The moment you reach level 3 with Q+W+E online, watch for him to step up to bomb the wave — drop Frozen Domain on him immediately, Pillar of Ice behind him to cut the retreat, then run him down with the movement speed bonus from W. This is your narrowest gap in the entire lane and you must punish it hard or surrender all initiative.
edits.after: At levels 1-2 you are farming under a bomb barrage — Bouncing Bomb reaches 850 against Chomp's 300, and Short Fuse fires an empowered auto whose cooldown shortens every time he casts, so contesting the same spot is punished twice over. Accept it. Chomp the wave for King's Tribute healing, and stand so the bomb has to arc over minions to reach you. The moment you hit level 3, watch for him to step up to bomb — Frozen Domain on him, Pillar of Ice across his line, then run him down on the move speed. One caution the rest of this page gets wrong: Satchel Charge knocks Ziggs clear as well as you, and it is 20 seconds at rank 1, so the window only opens once he has spent it.

edits.before: Levels 4-5 are genuinely awful. Ziggs can stand at max range and drop Hexplosive Minefield directly on the path between you, so any walk-up to drop Frozen Domain means eating the full zone tick damage before you even reach him. Respect this window, shove the wave with Q and passive healing when possible, and keep your HP above 65% — he is looking for a setup where you are low enough that the damage from his Q and E kills you before you close range. At level 6 everything changes: walk at him with Subjugate already charged, drop Frozen Domain, and Pillar the exit. He has no dash, no invulnerability, no mobility spell — once Subjugate fires the first cast he loses half his MR immediately and you gain it, making you dramatically harder to kill in the very moment he needs his AP to matter.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 are genuinely awful. Ziggs stands at 900 range and drops Hexplosive Minefield across the path between you, so every walk-up costs health before you arrive — though successive detonations on the same target deal reduced damage, which makes a straight line through the field cheaper than picking around it. Shove with Chomp and King's Tribute healing where you can, and hold above 65%. At level 6 everything changes: walk at him with Subjugate ready, Frozen Domain down, Pillar on the exit. What he does have is Satchel Charge — 20 seconds at rank 1, and it knocks him clear as well as you — so start after he spends it. Then R takes 40% of his MR and a fifth of his max health, healed straight back into your own bar.

edits.before: Ziggs at two items is a siege engine you cannot answer in a straight line. He pushes waves to your tower from a screen away, the Hexplosive Minefield makes any bush or chokepoint a death trap, and his Mega Inferno Bomb provides global pressure that forces you off any objective contest. Your only functional role is to use your now-substantial resistances from Iceborn Gauntlet plus Subjugate's drain to peel for your backline or hard-dive him in a 5v5 chaos fight where he cannot kite freely. If you snowballed the level 6 window into a kill and a lead, you can still be relevant by denying his ability to siege isolated towers; if you did not, accept that Ziggs wins the macro and build for team-fight impact over a duel you cannot force.
edits.after: Ziggs at two items is a siege engine you cannot answer in a straight line. He pushes waves to your tower from a screen away, Hexplosive Minefield turns any chokepoint into a toll, and Mega Inferno Bomb reaches 5000 units on a 120-second cooldown for global pressure. Your functional role is to use the resistances Iceborn Gauntlet and Subjugate give you to peel for your backline or hard-dive him in a 5v5 where he cannot kite. Subjugate is worth more on him than instinct suggests: a fifth of his max health plus the same again as healing is a lot on that frame. If you snowballed level 6, deny his isolated sieges; if not, build for team fights over a duel you cannot force.

notes: The two layers of this matchup disagree about whether Ziggs can escape at all. The full layer correctly tracks Satchel Charge as his self-peel; the content layer says in two places that he has "no dash, no invulnerability, no mobility spell" and "no defensive ability to escape the drain". Riot's text is unambiguous — the explosion knocks Ziggs away too and he takes no damage — so the content layer is sending a Trundle into a level-6 all-in that Satchel Charge answers for free. Second useful correction: Hexplosive Minefield's successive detonations on the same target deal reduced damage, which means walking a straight line through the field is cheaper than the page's advice to avoid the approach entirely. Deliberate non-propagation: _missing-interactions.json raises resistances-invalidated for Ziggs off a percentHealth flag on Satchel Charge, but Riot's description attaches the percentage language to hexploding turrets, not champions — I trusted the description and wrote nothing about him bypassing resistances.
